schema_purpose: Working intermediate schema for a guqin (jianzipu-style) note-event corpus fixture. Not the project's eventual cross-tradition notation format -- that is a separate future effort. This schema exists only to make the source-given/interpretive distinction explicit and machine-checkable.

piece.anthology_compiler: Zhu Quan (朱權), Prince of Ning
piece.content_status: The piece identity and anthology metadata above are real, documented facts (see source-note.md). The note_events in every section below are INVENTED for this fixture -- they illustrate the schema and the documented macro-form, and must not be treated as a reproduction of the 1425 print or of any specific modern dapu (reconstruction) recording.

notation_conventions.string_numbering: Strings numbered 1 (thickest, lowest-pitched, 一弦) through 7 (thinnest, highest-pitched, 七弦) -- real jianzipu convention.

position_types.stopped: 按音 (anyin) -- string pressed to a hui position with the left hand and plucked.
position_types.harmonic: 泛音 (fanyin) -- string lightly touched at a hui node and released at the moment of plucking, producing a harmonic overtone.

notation_conventions.hui_system: 13 hui (徽) position markers inlaid along the string's length, real convention. Only hui 7 (the exact midpoint) is used here with an acoustically confident pitch consequence (see pitch_interpretive_policy) -- other hui values appear as position labels only, without a claimed pitch derivation.
notation_conventions.duration_policy: Real jianzipu does not specify rhythm. The 'duration' field below is honestly 'unspecified' for every note in this fixture -- this is not a gap to be filled with a default, it is the documented state of the source notation.
notation_conventions.pitch_interpretive_policy: Real jianzipu does not specify absolute pitch directly; pitch is a physical consequence of string + position + the player's chosen tuning, transmitted separately from the tablature by oral/performance tradition. The 'pitch_interpretive' field is populated ONLY where it can be derived with reasonable confidence from the stated tuning below (open strings directly; the hui-7 octave harmonic, which is the one hui-to-interval fact this fixture treats as reliable). Everywhere else it is left null with an explanatory status string, rather than guessed.

tuning.name: zhengdiao (正調) / 'standard' tuning -- illustrative anchor only
tuning.caveat: Guqin has no single historically fixed absolute pitch standard; the reference pitch below (string 1 = C3, MIDI 48) is a common modern convention, chosen here only so this fixture's interpretive layer has something concrete to compute from, not as a claim about how the piece was historically pitched.
